why: Same notions. The project's IsStrongBundleRetraction and B's IsStrongBundleRetractionB agree for U relatively open (B's [1]-map is any sc-smooth lift Φ₁, the project's is shiftFiber R; they agree on U ⊕ F₁, so sc-smoothness transfers by IsScSmooth.congr), hence IsStrongBundleRetract = B's local strong bundle retract; strongLevel/strongShiftOne are B's KcapB/KoneB and the base retract r(U) is B's baseB definitionally. A ⇒ B: K_{m,k} = {u ∈ O_m, Γ(u,h) = h} is mem_image_iff at (ι_m u, ι_k h) (for all k, not only k ≤ m+1); the K[0], K[1] level descriptions add prod_toBase/shiftScale_toBase; p : K[i] → O sc-smooth is isScSmoothRetractMap_fst(_one) + isScRetract(_one) with base K = r(U). B ⇒ A: mem_image_iff is B's K_{0,0} formula; isScRetract(_one), isScSmoothRetractMap_fst(_one) come from B's existential Definition 2.7 for p : K[i] → O (via isScSmoothRetractMap_iff_exists); shiftIncl composes the sc-operator E ⊕ F¹ → E ⊕ F with B's retraction onto K[1]. toScRetractionOne_retract is about the project's internal retraction shiftFiber R (which B cannot name) and is re-proved set-theoretically from the definitions, using B's K[1] description for one inclusion.
